constraints: bounded intervals only; convert inequality -> interval and test one endpoint; integer endpoints
hints: Find both boundary numbers and decide which endpoint includes equality.
Write the smaller boundary first; use a parenthesis for strict and a bracket for inclusive.
Test the indicated endpoint against the original comparison to confirm its mark.

constraints: single rays both directions; infinity always gets a round bracket; convert both ways
hints: Identify whether the input is an inequality or an interval, and note whether its ray extends left toward negative infinity or right toward positive infinity.
Keep infinity beside a parenthesis. Transfer finite-endpoint inclusion between <= or >= and a square bracket, and exclusion between < or > and a parenthesis.
Convert to the notation the question requests: write an interval for an inequality input, or a variable comparison for an interval input.

constraints: two-piece unions from 'or' inequalities; at most two solving steps per piece; convert both ways
hints: If an input branch is not already isolated, solve its linear inequality first and preserve or reverse its comparison as the operation requires.
For each isolated ray, preserve its finite endpoint and inclusion while converting in the requested direction: comparison to interval, or interval to comparison in the named variable.
Join the two interval pieces with a union symbol, or join the two comparisons with OR, while preserving both endpoint rules.

constraints: cost model with a cap; integer boundary
hints: Let a whole-number variable count the actual purchasable item, and include any fixed one-time cost in the total.
Write an at-most inequality for the cap, subtract the fixed cost if present, and divide by the positive per-item amount.
Choose the greatest allowed whole count at or below the boundary, then check that its total stays within the cap.

constraints: at-least targets; averages or savings
hints: Define the requested unknown, which may be a score, count, time, or another accumulated quantity; for an average target, multiply the target average by the final number of values.
Model the named total or average with an inclusive lower-bound inequality and isolate the unknown.
If the question requires a whole count or whole time, choose the smallest whole value at or above the boundary; otherwise retain the exact continuous boundary, then check it in the original model.

constraints: whole-number contexts; round down for at-most caps
hints: Separate any existing load or fixed fee from the part contributed by each additional item.
Subtract that fixed part from the allowed total, then divide the remaining capacity by the positive amount per item.
Round down to a whole-item capacity when needed and verify that the resulting total does not exceed the limit.

constraints: less-than gives a bounded interval
hints: Read absolute value as distance from zero.
Distances smaller than the positive bound lie between the matching negative and positive boundaries.
Write that bounded region with endpoint marks determined by the inequality symbol.

constraints: greater-than gives two rays
hints: Interpret the absolute value as distance from zero and identify the positive boundary distance, regardless of which side of the written comparison contains the absolute value.
A greater-than distance condition selects the two outside rays. Include the boundary values for >= and exclude them for >.
Write the low and high rays as a union, preserving the strict or inclusive endpoint marks in the requested notation.

constraints: negative right-hand side only
hints: Recall that every absolute value is at least zero, while the displayed bound is negative.
A request for an absolute value below a negative number is impossible, whether the comparison is strict or inclusive.
A request for an absolute value above a negative number holds for every real input, whether the comparison is strict or inclusive; classify each displayed case from its direction.

constraints: linear inside; bounded interval answers
hints: Rewrite the inside absolute-value expression between the negative and positive bounds, keeping the original strictness or inclusion.
Undo the inside addition or subtraction across all three sections, then divide by its coefficient. Reverse both comparisons when that coefficient is negative, as in an expression such as 4-x.
Restore the endpoints to increasing order and write the bounded interval with parentheses for strict endpoints or brackets for included endpoints.

constraints: two-ray answers; keep the union
hints: After isolating the absolute value, split a greater-than condition into one branch below the negative bound and one above the positive bound.
Solve each linear branch; reverse a comparison only when multiplying or dividing that branch by a negative number.
Keep the two outside regions as a union, including both endpoints for >= and excluding both for >.

constraints: isolate the absolute value before splitting into cases
hints: First isolate the absolute value by undoing every outside constant and coefficient, and note the resulting comparison direction and threshold.

For a positive threshold, a less-than condition gives a bounded region while a greater-than condition gives two outside rays; check nonpositive thresholds against the fact that absolute value is never negative.
Solve the resulting linear bound or branches and preserve strict endpoints with parentheses and inclusive endpoints with brackets.

constraints: solid for <= or >=; dashed for < or >
hints: Use the equality version of the line as the boundary.
Check whether the inequality symbol has an equal bar.
Choose the boundary style that includes points on the line only when equality is permitted.

objective: Test a point to choose the shaded side
constraints: substitute a test point; true -> shade that side
hints: Substitute the point's x- and y-coordinates into the inequality.
Evaluate both sides and compare the resulting numbers.
The point belongs precisely when that numerical comparison is true.

constraints: the origin is the easiest test point unless it is on the line
hints: Test the origin by putting x = 0 and y = 0 into the inequality.
Compare zero with the resulting constant side.
Use that true-or-false result to decide whether the origin lies in the shaded half-plane.

objective: Verify a pair in both equations
constraints: check the point in BOTH equations
hints: Substitute the proposed coordinates into the first equation and subtract its right side from its left side.
Repeat that residual calculation for the second equation.
Both residuals must be zero for the proposed pair to solve the system.

objective: Reject a pair that fails one equation
constraints: one equation passes, the other fails
hints: Compute a left-minus-right residual for each equation at the proposed pair.
Find which residual is nonzero; that equation rejects the pair.
Report both residuals before deciding whether both equations hold.

constraints: two candidates; exactly one works
hints: Test one candidate in both equations rather than relying on one equation alone.
If it fails, test the other candidate the same way.
Choose the pair whose substitutions satisfy both equalities.

constraints: the intersection point is the solution
hints: Look for a point shared by both plotted lines or both tables; that common ordered pair is the graphical intersection.
If the lines are given by formulas instead, set their y-values equal at the intersection and solve for the common x-coordinate.
Find the corresponding y-coordinate from either representation and verify that the ordered pair lies on both lines.

constraints: standard form, slope-intercept, and horizontal/vertical lines
hints: Identify each line form: a vertical line fixes x, a horizontal line fixes y, and a standard or slope-intercept equation relates both coordinates.
Use any fixed coordinate directly; otherwise rewrite or combine the two equations to find one coordinate of their crossing.
Substitute to find the other coordinate and check the ordered pair in both original line equations.

constraints: an estimate must be checked in both equations
hints: Substitute the estimated coordinates into each equation separately.
Calculate each left-minus-right residual exactly.
Only zero residuals in both equations confirm the graphical estimate.

constraints: one equation already solved for a variable; integer solutions
hints: Replace the isolated variable in the other equation with its expression.
Solve the resulting equation in one variable.
Back-substitute for the second coordinate and check both original equations.

constraints: both equations solved for y; set them equal
hints: Since both expressions equal y, set their right sides equal.
Solve that equation for x before finding y from either expression.
Use the unused expression to verify the ordered pair.

constraints: verify the pair in the equation not used for back-substitution
hints: Identify which variable is already isolated and substitute its entire signed expression into the other equation.
Solve for the remaining variable, then use the isolated equation to recover the first variable.
Verify the ordered pair in both originals, especially the equation that was not used for back-substitution.
